title: fix(synology-chat): resolve its unused-type CI failure
body:
Related: [scheduled main CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39805986795/job/119919727179).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Synology Chat's unused-export failure in scheduled main CI.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. The webhook-path union and resolved account property stay intact; no public SDK, configuration, dependency, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the webhook-path source alias private to its defining file. Its only consumer is the resolved account type in that same file, and none of the plugin's public entry points exports it. This follows the existing plugin boundary rather than adding an ignore or a fabricated consumer.

The complete change removes one export keyword. No tests or production behavior are changed; no new scaffolding is needed.

## Evidence

- Pinned Knip 6.40.0 with the canonical production and full-tree configurations, scoped to `extensions/synology-chat`: each reproduces exactly `SynologyWebhookPathSource` on base, then passes with zero findings after the repair. Base wall times: 31.17s / 41.50s; repaired: 29.21s / 43.65s. These are scoped results, not a claim that the repository-wide deadcode gate is green.
- Package-boundary typecheck passes after the canonical SDK declaration preparation; one-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The initial unprepared typecheck failed on missing SDK declarations and is not counted as a product failure or a passing check.
- `pnpm test:extension synology-chat --maxWorkers=1`: **165 passed / 1 failed**, 86.14s wall including cold worker preparation. The identical `client.loopback.test.ts:169` retry assertion independently reproduces on the clean base with the same command/order: **165 passed / 1 failed**, 24.68s wall. This unrelated failure is retained, not fixed, skipped, retried away, or relabeled green. Hosted test-specific CI seconds are not isolated.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the exact one-token patch and intact plugin boundary/public-entry context completed with no actionable findings. No visual change.
- Publication-base integration was required by an actual non-fast-forward refusal; range-diff confirms the patch is identical. The Synology files, public barrels, Knip configurations/pin manifest, and package-boundary configuration are unchanged, so their scoped proof is reused.
- Direct main publication was then rejected by GH013 because changes require a pull request. This PR follows that ruleset; no CI dispatch or rerun was requested.

Co-authored with @vincentkoc.
